chunks: And Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz, from Yazid al-Kunasī, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the divorce of the pregnant woman, and he said: 'She is divorced once for the waiting period with witnesses.' I said: 'Does he have the right to take her back?' He said: 'Yes, and she is still his wife.' I said: 'If he took her back and had intercourse with her, then intended to divorce her with another divorce,' he said: 'He does not divorce her until a month passes after he had intercourse with her.' I said: 'If he divorced her a second time and testified, then took her back and testified to her return and had intercourse with her, then divorced her with the third divorce and testified to her divorce for each waiting period being a month, does she become fully divorced from him just as the woman divorced once becomes fully divorced, who does not become permissible to her husband until she marries another husband?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'What is her waiting period?' He said: 'Her waiting period is that she gives birth to what is in her belly, then she becomes permissible to the husbands.'

key_terms.تَبِينُ مِنْهُ: She becomes fully divorced from him
key_terms.تَضَعُ مَا فِي بَطْنِهَا: She gives birth to what is in her belly

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period and divorce procedure for a pregnant woman in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Isfahani's chain within al-Istibsar, this hadith details the procedural nuances of talaq for a pregnant woman, emphasizing that the waiting period (iddah) extends until childbirth as per the consensus of Shia jurists. It clarifies that a single divorce allows for revocation during the iddah, while a triple divorce results in final separation (talaq mubarramah), requiring a subsequent marriage to a third party before the first husband can remarry her.
